reason: The cited evidence (E1) discusses SFE and twinning in the CoCrNi medium entropy alloy, not in the Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy or the baseline CoCrFeMnNi. It provides no data on the effect of Co removal on SFE, the temperature/strain-rate dependence of SFE in FeNiCrMn, or comparative deformation mechanisms. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: Removing Co from CoCrFeMnNi alters the stacking fault energy (SFE) of the resulting FeNiCrMn alloy.
The SFE of FeNiCrMn is temperature- and strain-rate-dependent, decreasing at low temperatures/high rates and increasing at high temperatures/low rates.
A reduced SFE promotes deformation twinning, which enhances strain hardening and ductility.
An increased SFE favors dislocation glide with dynamic recovery, reducing strain hardening.
The equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy has a lower SFE and thus less temperature-/rate-dependent variation in deformation mechanism.
